title: Cerulean Health — Token Economics Realignment and Ops Runbook
content:
Summary:
This note synthesizes the before/after cost model for Cerulean Health after applying Redwood Optimize recommendations. Goal: reduce hosted inference spend while keeping end-to-end latency within clinical SLAs (p95 <= 600ms) and maintaining answer quality (narrow QA regression margin < 2% on the evaluation set). This is a working doc for the product + solutions handoff and the pilot rollout plan.

Customer profile (short):
- Company: Cerulean Health (digital triage + clinical summarization).
- Primary workload: conversational triage + discharge summary generation + embeddings for patient search.
- Traffic: bursty weekday peaks 10:00–16:00 PST; baseline 1.2k reqs/minute peak, average 330 reqs/minute.
- Average tokens per request: 420 input + 210 output = 630 tokens total.

Baseline (observed, month M):
- Endpoint: hosted-api /generate (model: open-llm-13b-fp32-standard)
- Monthly requests: 1.6M
- Monthly tokens: ~1.0B tokens (sum of input+output)
- Average latency (p50/p95): 180ms / 540ms
- Current monthly inference cost (raw): $81,200
- Current observed failure rate (5xx): 0.6%
- Cache hit-rate: ~2% (user-level dedupe only)

Key constraints noted by Cerulean:
- Cannot accept >10% quality drift on clinical summarization prompts (QA metric tracked in JIRA-CH-1022).
- Data residency: US-only (no cross-region fallbacks).
- Nightly batch processing must retain current throughput window (00:00–04:00 PST).

Redwood Optimize recommendations applied in this scenario (short):
1) Model variant swap: open-llm-13b -> open-llm-13b-int8-opt (int8 quantized variant validated on eval set).
2) Smart prefix KV cache: enable per-patient prompt prefix caching for templates; expected cache effectiveness for triage prompts.
3) Dynamic batching with latency SLO: enable small-window continuous batching with p95 latency guard 600ms.
4) Tail routing: route low-priority nightly batch traffic to lower-cost capacity pool (reserved burst instances).
5) Embedding caching + vector dedupe: cache embeddings for repeated patient queries across sessions for search workload.
6) Prompt rewrite suggestions: reduce average output length via templated truncation and controlled expanders (ops to try 10% output reduction guardrails).

Before/After modeled numbers (consolidated):
- Baseline monthly tokens: 1,000,000,000
- Baseline monthly cost: $81,200

- After Optimize (conservative projection):
  - Quantization savings (int8 runtime): 28% of model compute cost -> direct token-cost reduction estimated 23% overall
  - KV cache & embedding cache combined: reduces served token load by 17% (prefixes + duplicate embedding lookups)
  - Dynamic batching efficiency: reduces per-token overhead by 12% (effective kernel/pipeline utilization)
  - Prompt length tightening: reduces output tokens by 9% (applied only to non-critical summaries)
  - Nightly reroute savings: moves 18% of tokens to a 40% cheaper pool for off-peak work

- Modeled After totals (conservative consolidated):
  - Effective tokens served (post-caches & trimming): 1,000,000,000 * (1 - 0.17 - 0.09) = 740,000,000 tokens (note: apply quantization and batching on remaining)
  - Effective unit cost reduction from quantization + batching: ~35% multiplier on cost per token
  - Projected monthly cost (conservative): ~$29,800
  - Projected absolute savings: ~$51,400 per month (~63% reduction)

Notes on modeling approach and assumptions:
- All savings calculations are multiplicative where appropriate (cache reduces tokens served; quantization reduces computational cost per token).
- We used Cerulean traffic histogram provided in gs://redwood-benchmarks/cerulean-health-embed-samples-2025q4 and applied Redwood's kernel-level perf numbers for the int8 runtime (bench: int8 throughput uplift 2.8x vs fp32 on target A100 class hardware for this model family).
- Assumed no model quality regression after int8 validation run; validation artifacts in github.com/redwood/optimize/pull/189. If we observe >2% QA regression, rollback quantized model for the summarization route and keep quantization for embeddings/search-only workload.

Sensitivity table (high-level):
- If cache hit-rate is 10% lower than expected -> projected savings drop to ~49% (monthly cost ~$41,300).
- If output trimming causes user-visible errors requiring re-generation for 4% of requests -> net savings reduce by ~7 percentage points.

Quality guardrails and metrics to monitor: (to be added to the route dashboard)
- Cost / 1M tokens (baseline vs live)
- p50/p95 latency per route (canary vs baseline)
- QA pass rate on sampled clinical summaries (daily sampling, 500 samples) -> tracked in JIRA-CH-1022
- Error rate (5xx) and user fallback rate (client re-tries)
- Cache hit rate (prefix + embeddings) and TVS (tokens-avoided) metric

Rollout plan (phased):
- Week 0: Prepilot (QA + bench)
  - Run int8 validation on historical eval set (owner: Ibrahim). Validation artifact: github.com/redwood/optimize/pull/189
  - Collect bench latencies on dedicated test pool (owner: SRE)
- Week 1: Canary (1% traffic)
  - Enable quantized model for non-critical routes (embeddings + triage read-only) + enable KV cache with TTL 2h
  - Monitor QA and latency for 72h; rollback trigger: QA drop >2% or p95 increase >20% absolute
- Week 2–3: Ramp to 20% (A/B split)
  - Add dynamic batching on the canary pool; ensure p95 <= 600ms for user-facing flows
  - Enable nightly reroute for scheduled jobs (off-peak)
- Week 4: Full rollout (subject to signoff)
  - Apply prompt trimming in production with conservative guardrails and observability hooks

Operational runbook (checklist):
- Pre-deploy:
  - Snapshot baseline cost-report (Finance). File: shared_drives/product/optimize/cerulean-health-cost-model-baseline-202511.xlsx (note: copy exists in customer's secure workspace).
  - Confirm KMS keys for private model variants (security signoff required).
- Deploy steps (rolling):
  1) Deploy quantized variant to canary pool with traffic tag 'cerulean-int8-canary'. (deploy PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/1420)
  2) Toggle KV cache setting for route '/generate' -> prefix-cache:on, ttl=120min.
  3) Enable batching config profile 'cerulean-small-window' with max_delay=8ms, max_batch_size=32.
  4) Configure fallback policy: if p95 latency or 5xx spikes beyond thresholds, route to original model (automatic in canary config).
- Post-deploy monitoring and actions:
  - Daily digest to Cerulean ops slack channel with cost delta and QA sample results (owner: Claire).
  - Weekly review for 4 weeks between Redwood CS and Cerulean engineering to validate downstream effects.

Risk register (short):
- Risk: Quality regression in clinical summarization from quantization or trimming. Mitigation: A/B sample evaluation; automatic traffic rollback triggers; preserve non-quantized model for critical route.
- Risk: Unexpected latency regressions under burst. Mitigation: conservative batching settings + autoscale headroom.
- Risk: Lower than expected cache hit-rate. Mitigation: iterate on prompt normalization and template stitching; increase TTL for safe templates.

Action items (next steps / owners):
- Ibrahim: finalize int8 validation report and attach artifacts to CONFLUENCE-CH-4532 (due 2025-11-21).
- Claire: create canary dashboard and add health checks/alerts (due 2025-11-24).
- Ari: update customer-facing proposal with explicit SLA language and rollback commitments (due 2025-11-26).
- Maya: schedule kickoff with Cerulean on 2025-11-30 (include SRE and Solutions eng).

Appendix: quick worksheet layout (sheet tabs referenced in the internal spreadsheet)
- traffic-profile: hourly histogram and sequence length distribution
- cost-model: line items (model compute, I/O, embedding ops, routing overhead)
- scenario-compare: baseline vs conservative vs optimistic vs pessimistic
- rollout-checklist: detailed operational steps and contact list

Notes and provenance:
- Numbers in this doc derived from Cerulean provided usage export (export id: cerulean-usage-202510.csv), Redwood microbenchmarks for the int8 runtime, and historical batching experiments from infra/bench/2025-q3.
- This is intentionally conservative; if cache behavior and quantization both behave at the optimistic end, savings could approach ~75% monthly reduction but we will not promise that in the customer-facing summary without full pilot results.

END OF DOC
